verdict.rationale: Cline Kanban is documented for running many coding agents in parallel from a web task board, with per-card isolated git worktrees, auto-commit and dependency chains. YOLO/auto-approve and headless CLI modes allow agents to act without prompts. Nothing documents agents sustaining work for hours or days: scheduled agents that persist across restarts are a recurring cron feature, not long-running sessions, and subagents are in-task research helpers. missing for 10: evidence of multi-hour/multi-day continuous agent runs, documented scale limits for agent fleets, independent hands-on corroboration of parallel Kanban fleets.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can launch fleets of autonomous agents that work in parallel on different tasks for hours or days

citations.quote: Run many agents in parallel from a web-based task board with per-card worktrees, auto-commit, and dependency chains.
Use Cline Kanban to run multiple coding agents in parallel with isolated git worktrees.
Autonomous execution can modify files and run commands without further prompts.
Check the box and Cline auto-approves everything: file changes, terminal commands, browser actions, MCP tools, and mode transitions.
